title: The symmetric algebra commutes with base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module, with symmetric algebras $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$, $\iota_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ and $\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$, $\iota_{S\otimes M}$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $\beta:\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$ be the $R$-algebra homomorphism with $\beta(\iota_M(m))=\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)$. Then the $S$-algebra homomorphism $S\otimes_R\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\,\beta(a)$, is an isomorphism. (For $S=R_f$ the localization at the powers of $f\in R$: $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)_f\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{R_f}(M_f)$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F (label lemma-tensor-algebra-localization, line 2386; localization of tensor and symmetric algebras, with proof omitted and hint to Lemma 00DE) and Lemma 00DE (label lemma-tensor-product-localization, line 2124); the general base change follows from the universal properties: for a commutative S-algebra B, Hom_{S-alg}(S⊗_R Sym_R M, B) = Hom_{R-alg}(Sym_R M, B) = Hom_R(M, B) = Hom_S(S⊗_R M, B) = Hom_{S-alg}(Sym_S(S⊗_R M), B), compatibly with the map of the statement

proof.text: Let $A_R=\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ and $A_S=\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$. By the universal property of the symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], the $R$-linear map $m\mapsto\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)$ induces the unique $R$-algebra map $\beta:A_R\to A_S$ appearing in the statement. The map is well defined because the displayed map is $R$-linear: the scalar action on $A_S$ is restricted along $R\to S$ and $1\otimes(rm)=r(1\otimes m)$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM and Lemma 0C6F; construction of the map on generators

proof.text: The $S$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi:S\otimes_RA_R\to A_S$ is the inverse image of $\beta$ under the base-change universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property]. Explicitly, $\Phi(s\otimes a)=s\,\beta(a)$, and in particular $\Phi(1\otimes\iota_M(m))=\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)$.

Let $j:M\to S\otimes_RA_R$ be $m\mapsto1\otimes\iota_M(m)$. The module base-change universal property [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property] gives a unique $S$-linear map $\widetilde j:S\otimes_RM\to S\otimes_RA_R$ with $\widetilde j(s\otimes m)=s\otimes\iota_M(m)$. Applying the universal property of $A_S$ to $\widetilde j$ gives an $S$-algebra homomorphism $\Psi:A_S\to S\otimes_RA_R$ satisfying $\Psi(\iota_{S\otimes M}(s\otimes m))=s\otimes\iota_M(m)$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM and Lemma 0C6F; universal property applied after extension of scalars

proof.text: The composite $\Phi\circ\Psi$ is the identity on $A_S$: on each generator $\iota_{S\otimes M}(s\otimes m)$, the formula for $\Psi$ followed by the formula for $\Phi$ gives $s\,\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)=\iota_{S\otimes M}(s\otimes m)$, and the uniqueness clause of the symmetric-algebra universal property makes the two $S$-algebra maps equal.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F, equality of maps by the universal property

proof.text: The composite $\Psi\circ\Phi$ is the identity on $S\otimes_RA_R$. By the base-change universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property], it suffices to compare the restrictions of these $S$-algebra maps along $A_R\to S\otimes_RA_R$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Their restrictions are $\Psi\circ\beta$ and $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. These are equal by the uniqueness clause of the symmetric-algebra universal property: on $\iota_M(m)$ both give $1\otimes\iota_M(m)$, because $\beta(\iota_M(m))=\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)$ and $\Psi$ has the displayed generator formula. Thus $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F, equality of maps by the two universal properties

proof.text: For $S=R_f$, apply the isomorphism just proved and then the canonical tensor-localization identifications from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor]: $R_f\otimes_R\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)_f$ and $R_f\otimes_RM\cong M_f$. Under these identifications the comparison is exactly $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)_f\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{R_f}(M_f)$, with the stated map on pure tensors.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F and Lemma 00DE, localization case
